[RCLI.1.7] **`strip-debug` removes an artefact's debug metadata.** It reads a
`.dsc` and writes to the path `-o` names the same artefact without its `DsSource`,
`LineSpan`, `DocString`, `RuleSource` and `RuleDebugName` atoms — source text, source spans, docstrings,
rule source locations and debug display names ([RDSC.7.1]). An engine executes
the stripped artefact exactly as it executes the original; what is lost is what
a debugger or a documentation tool reads.

A compiler must not strip an atom whose absence changes execution. A rule with
no `RuleCooldown` atom has no cooldown ([RDSC.6.5.4]), so `RuleCooldown` is kept, although it
is per-rule metadata in form.
